text: Dawn came gentle over the hills. She breathed deeply, and for the first time in months, hope felt possible again.
label: Light / hopeful
convention: Explicit hope plus a softening, optimistic image (gentle dawn) reads as light/hopeful to any reader; naive list counts hope+gentle.

text: She held the sleeping baby against her chest, calm and tender, and the whole world went quiet and soft around them.
label: Warm
convention: A tender, intimate domestic moment is warm rather than soaring; naive counts calm+tender and over-shoots the ratio into Light/hopeful.

text: My dear friend, I think of you often and warmly. The garden you planted years ago still blooms by the gate.
label: Warm
convention: Affectionate, settled feeling toward a friend is the textbook 'Warm'; naive counts 'warm' once for a matching ratio.

text: They sat at the conference table and worked through the quarterly figures. The report was due Thursday and the printer was low on toner.
label: Balanced
convention: Flat, affect-neutral procedural prose with no emotional charge is Balanced; naive finds no list words and returns Balanced.

text: He ran. The footsteps behind him did not stop. Somewhere a door slammed, his lungs burned, and his pulse hammered against his ribs.
label: Tense / somber
convention: Chase, pursuit and panic read as tense; naive misses it because 'ran/footsteps/slammed/pulse' aren't in the English negative list, so it returns Balanced.

text: Darkness. Grief. The blood on the snow would not wash away, and a cold dread coiled in every shadow of the dead house.
label: Dark / ominous
convention: Dense imagery of death, grief and dread is unmistakably dark; naive counts dark+grief+blood+cold+dread+shadow.

text: There was no hope left in him. The fire had gone out long ago, and only grey ash remained where a man used to be.
label: Dark / ominous
convention: 'No hope left' is a despairing, hollowed-out statement (dark); naive ignores the negation, counts 'hope' as positive, and labels it Warm.

text: Without fear, she smiled at the storm, squared her shoulders, and stepped out onto the swaying bridge.
label: Light / hopeful
convention: Negated fear plus a smile and bold forward action is positive/courageous; naive counts 'fear' negative and 'smile' positive, they cancel, yielding Balanced.

text: Without fear and without hate, the knight rode straight into the enemy line, calm as still water at first light.
label: Light / hopeful
convention: Both 'fear' and 'hate' are explicitly negated and the actor is 'calm', so the felt tone is serene resolve; naive counts both negatives literally but 'calm' and 'light' offset them, so the ratio cancels to 0 and it returns Balanced.

text: "You don't love me," she said. It wasn't a question. He looked at the floor and found nothing there worth saying.
label: Tense / somber
convention: A quiet breakup with a negated 'love' is somber; naive counts 'love' positive despite the 'don't' and mislabels it Warm.

text: Lightning split the dark sky. The cold rain hammered the broken road, and the wind dragged a shutter back and forth.
label: Tense / somber
convention: An ominous storm is moody/tense but not death-laden; naive substring-counts 'dark','cold','broken' (and a phantom 'light' inside 'lightning') and over-rates it to Dark/ominous.

text: "Don't scold the boy," his mother said, though her voice stayed level and her hands kept folding the warm laundry.
label: Warm
convention: A mild, caring domestic scene reads warm; naive finds a phantom 'cold' inside 'scold' that cancels the real 'warm', netting a zero ratio and Balanced.

text: "I lost my keys again," she laughed, and we turned the whole bright little apartment upside down hunting for them.
label: Warm
convention: A playful, affectionate everyday scene is warm; naive counts 'lost' negative against 'bright' positive, they cancel to Balanced.

text: After seven years of war, the two nations signed the peace. Bells rang across the city; strangers wept and embraced in the square.
label: Light / hopeful
convention: Public joy and relief at war's end is elating/hopeful; naive only catches 'peace' once, so the ratio under-shoots the Light threshold and stops at Warm.

text: They lowered the coffin into the wet earth. The rain was soft. No one spoke, because there was nothing left to say.
label: Tense / somber
convention: A hushed funeral is plainly somber; naive finds none of its list words (grief/death absent as tokens) and returns Balanced.

text: "If you ever come back here," the old man whispered, leaning close, "you will not leave again with your life."
label: Dark / ominous
convention: A whispered death threat is menacing/ominous; naive matches no list tokens (no 'death/blood/kill') and returns Balanced.

text: Oh, perfect. Just perfect. The car was dead, the rain was endless, and her phone had already drowned in the gutter.
label: Tense / somber
convention: Ironic 'perfect' over a string of small disasters reads as frustrated/grim, not positive; naive sees no positive list words but the phantom 'death' inside 'dead' is absent (it is a separate token), so it returns Balanced.

text: "This is going to be great," he announced with a grin, though dread sat low in his stomach like a swallowed stone.
label: Tense / somber
convention: Cheerful surface undercut by 'dread' is anxious; a reader weights the felt dread over the bravado. Naive also lands Tense via the single 'dread'.

text: It was a cruel little joke, the funny kind, the kind that leaves a bruise nobody else can see.
label: Tense / somber
convention: 'Funny' is overridden by 'cruel' and a hidden bruise; the lasting note is hurt. Naive counts 'cruel' and agrees.

text: Everything is fine. The water is rising in the basement, the dog won't stop barking, and the smoke alarm is singing. Everything is absolutely fine.
label: Tense / somber
convention: Repeated 'fine' over mounting alarm is sarcastic, signalling crisis; a reader reads escalating tension. Naive sees no list words and returns Balanced.

text: The sun was out. Somewhere a child laughed. He stood at the open grave with his hands in his pockets and felt absolutely nothing.
label: Tense / somber
convention: Bright surface details frame numb grief at a graveside; the dominant feeling is hollow/somber. Naive finds no tokens (no 'grief/death') and returns Balanced.

text: Het was een warme, lichte ochtend. De kinderen lachten in de tuin en de geur van vers brood dreef door het open raam.
label: Warm
convention: Dutch domestic-morning scene (warm light, laughing children, fresh bread) is warm; naive coincidentally matches the substring 'warm' in 'warme' and lands Warm.

text: De duisternis kwam. Niemand zou haar nog redden. Angst, kou, en bloed op de witte sneeuw.
label: Dark / ominous
convention: Dutch passage of darkness, fear, cold and blood on snow is dark; naive's English-only lists match nothing and it returns Balanced.

text: Hij liep naar het eind van de kade en keek naar het grijze water onder de lage hemel. De veerboot zou pas om zes uur komen.
label: Balanced
convention: Flat, observational Dutch prose with no emotional load is Balanced; naive matches nothing and agrees by accident.

text: Le feu crépitait doucement dans l'âtre. Les enfants riaient, et la maison tout entière était pleine de chaleur et de douceur.
label: Warm
convention: French fireside scene full of warmth and tenderness is warm; naive's English lists match no French tokens and it returns Balanced.

text: Il marcha jusqu'au bout du quai et regarda l'eau grise sous le ciel bas. Le train de midi avait dix minutes de retard.
label: Balanced
convention: Neutral French description with no affect is Balanced; naive matches nothing and agrees.

text: Il ne restait plus aucun espoir. La maison était froide, les lettres brûlées, et le silence pesait comme une pierre sur sa poitrine.
label: Dark / ominous
convention: French 'no hope left' in a cold, ash-and-silence scene is dark/despairing; naive's English lists catch nothing and return Balanced (and would miss the negation regardless).

text: Es war ein warmer, heller Tag. Die ganze Familie lachte am Tisch, und alles fühlte sich friedlich und leicht an.
label: Warm
convention: German family scene (warm, bright, peaceful, light) is warm; naive matches the substring 'warm' inside 'warmer' and lands Warm by coincidence.

text: Die Dunkelheit kam über das Dorf. Angst kroch durch die Gassen. Niemand würde sie retten in dieser kalten, toten Nacht.
label: Dark / ominous
convention: German night of darkness, fear and a 'dead' village is dark; naive's English lists match nothing and it returns Balanced.

text: La abuela sonrió y nos abrazó a todos. La casa entera olía a pan caliente, y por un momento nada más importaba.
label: Warm
convention: Spanish scene of a grandmother's embrace and fresh bread is warm; naive's English lists catch no Spanish tokens and return Balanced.

text: La sangre cubría el suelo de piedra. Nadie escaparía de aquella noche fría y muerta, y el miedo se cerró como una mano alrededor de su garganta.
label: Dark / ominous
convention: Spanish passage of blood, a 'dead' night, cold and throttling fear is dark; naive's English lists match nothing and return Balanced.
